title: Developer docs & Support runbook — canonical-fix matrix
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This runbook defines the operational bridge between Developer Docs (Docs Site) and Support for triaging recurring support cases into authoritative, reproducible, and minimally invasive "canonical fixes". The goal is to reduce time-to-resolution for customers, create a single source-of-truth for common fixes, and automate propagation from support ticket → docs patch → SDK/CLI sample → release.

Who this is for

- Support engineers handling customer issues tied to SDKs, APIs, and developer integrations.
- DX writers and Docs Engineers responsible for content updates and site releases.
- Engineers owning SDKs, runtimes, and server-side routes referenced in docs examples.

Scope and definitions

- Canonical fix: a tested, minimal change (docs + example code + if needed, an SDK patch) that resolves a repeatable support problem and becomes the definitive guidance for that failure mode.
- Repro harness: a lightweight, documented request/fixture that Support can run locally or against staging to reproduce an issue.
- Docs patch: the edited Confluence page + snippet update + commit to docs repo.

Ownership and roles

- Support (owner: customer-success): identifies candidate repeat issues and files an internal "canonical-fix request" via the Support Intake template (see step-by-step).
- Docs Engineering (owner: engineering): evaluates coverage, authors patch, runs local preview, and coordinates release.
- SDK Owner (owner: engineering): validates code examples, signs off on any suggested SDK changes.
- Release Manager (owner: engineering): schedules and publishes docs site release or emergency patch.

Quick intake checklist (Support)

1. Confirm reproducibility with customer or from logs. Capture: request id, timestamps, region, model, route, SDK version, exact request payload.
2. Run the small repro harness against Staging (if available). Attach the harness and outcome to the ticket.
3. If issue is reproducible and affects >1 customer or is likely to reoccur, create a Canonical-Fix Request issue in the internal tracker and tag Docs-OPS.

Canonical-Fix Request template (fields Support must fill)

- Title: short, action-oriented (e.g. "SDK: streaming resume fails on 401 with token-refresh flow").
- Symptom: one-sentence customer-facing description.
- Repro steps: numbered steps, include exact payload/headers.
- Repro harness: link to gist or internal snippet.
- Impact estimate: customers affected, severity (P0/P1/P2).
- Proposed docs change: suggested doc location & brief wording.
- Suggested owner: SDK or API service team.

Triage workflow (Docs Engineering)

1. Triage cadence: Docs-OPS triage meeting (Mon/Wed/Fri 09:30 ET) reviews all incoming canonical-fix requests older than 24h.
2. Assign owner: Docs Engineer assigns an author and an SDK/Service reviewer within 48 hours.
3. Draft patch: author prepares a minimal docs change, test harness, and example code.
4. Validation: SDK owner runs tests or performs manual validation. If a code change is required, create a linked SDK PR.
5. Release: either include the docs patch in the next scheduled docs deploy or apply an emergency patch following the emergency-patch checklist.

Mapping matrix (support symptom → docs page → canonical artifact)

Use the table below to capture the minimum required mapping for each canonical-fix request. Add rows to the internal tracking issue and link artifacts.

| Support symptom (short) | Owner team | Docs page (Confluence) | Repro harness (link) | Canonical snippet (file path) | SDK PR (if any) | Release path | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Streaming truncated on resume token error | eng-runtime | /confluence/eng-developer-experience/api-examples/streaming-fallback-patterns | gist:stream-resume-repro | snippets/stream-resume/fix-401.md | sdk-go#142 | Docs patch then SDK patch | Add telemetry sample |
| Embeddings drift on long batched inputs | eng-serving-runtime | /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/embeddings-batching-guide | gist:embed-batch-repro | snippets/embeds/batch-guidance.md | none | Docs-only in next patch | Include eval set |
| API 429 while bursting | eng-platform | /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/rate-limit-backoff | gist:429-repro | snippets/rate-limit/backoff-example.md | sdk-js#98 | Hotfix (if P0) | Add client retry header notes |

Rapid patch & rollback checklist

- When to hotpatch: customer-impacting P0 or P1 where docs provide incorrect guidance that causes data loss, security exposure, or major outage.
- Hotpatch steps (owner: Release Manager + Docs Eng + Support):
  1. Create minimal docs change branch named docs/hotfix/YYYYMMDD-issue-id.
  2. Include an explanatory changelog entry and mark the page with a red banner (see banner snippet below).
  3. Run local preview and smoke test examples against staging.
  4. Merge + publish with emergency pipeline.
  5. Post-publish: close the canonical-fix request with links to published page and release notes.
  6. If the change introduced regressions, rollback by reverting the commit and republishing.

Banner snippet (insert at top of Confluence page)

[!NOTE] This page was updated as an emergency fix on YYYY-MM-DD to address a customer-impacting issue (internal canonical-fix ID: CF-1234). See internal tracker: <internal-link>.

Sample CLI and Git workflow (Docs Engineers)

- Local preview (Dockerized docs site):

  ```bash
  # start local server
  make docs-serve
  # open preview URL printed by the command
  ```

- Create hotfix branch and cherry-pick

  ```bash
  git checkout -b docs/hotfix/CF-1234-20260301
  # edit page content (we keep snippets in docs/snippets/)
  git add docs/snippets/stream-resume/fix-401.md
  git commit -m "docs: CF-1234 fix streaming resume guidance"
  git push origin docs/hotfix/CF-1234-20260301
  # open PR and add reviewer: @sdk-owner @release-manager
  ```

Canonical fixes: examples

1) API sample fix (before / after)\n
- Before (incorrect):

  ```json
  {
    "model": "redwood-1",
    "stream": true,
    "resume_token": ""
  }
  ```

- After (canonical):

  ```json
  {
    "model": "redwood-1",
    "stream": true,
    "resume_token": null,
    "headers": {"Authorization": "Bearer <short-lived-token>"}
  }
  ```

2) SDK snippet fix (node)

  ```js
  // Wrong: silent swallow of 401 on resume
  sdk.streamResume(payload).catch(() => {});

  // Canonical: explicit refresh + retry
  try {
    await sdk.streamResume(payload);
  } catch (err) {
    if (err.code === 401) {
      await auth.refreshToken();
      await sdk.streamResume(payload);
    } else throw err;
  }
  ```

Observability & telemetry for docs-driven fixes

- Add a minimal telemetry event to the repro harness and canonical snippets: docs_issue_reported, docs_fix_applied, docs_validation_passed. These allow tracking time-to-fix and regression rates.
- Dashboard (Docs Ops):
  - Metric: number of canonical-fix requests opened / week. Target: <= 5 new unique requests per week after 3 months.
  - Metric: mean time from request → published docs patch. Target: <= 7 days (non-P0).
  - Metric: percentage of fixes that required SDK code change. Target: <= 30%.

KPIs and postmortem triggers

- A postmortem with engineering participation is required if any canonical-fix patch reverses or if customers report regression after the patch.
- If the same symptom reappears twice after a patch within 30 days, escalate to the Platform Quality initiative.
